title: The Broken Crossing
problem: A flood has ruined the road's only dependable crossing. Both banks claim the other neglected it.
material: The pier is scoured beneath the waterline.
testimony: Mara's ledger shows the repair crew was dismissed before inspection.
covenant: A witness mark was cut from the eastern stone.

options.name: Stone span
options.term: Quarry stone and two seasons of shared toll maintenance.
options.effect: Traffic steadies, but the quarry and poorer bank carry the first cost.

options.name: Shared ferry
options.term: Both banks must publicly renew their witness promise.
options.effect: Trade returns quickly, but passage depends on continued cooperation.

title: The Granary Road
problem: Flooded ruts strand grain carts while the upland farms ask who will yield dry ground.
material: Wheel cuts expose a failed drainage bed.
testimony: Farmers report that the old bypass was closed by a private gate.
covenant: The boundary stones once left room for seasonal water.

options.name: Raised causeway
options.term: Secure stone and guarantee public passage across the farms.
options.effect: Heavy carts move again, but building crews consume scarce stone.

options.name: Seasonal bypass
options.term: Return a strip of cropland to water and compensate its keeper.
options.effect: The road bends with the flood; the harvest loses a narrow field.

title: The Mill Sluice
problem: A mill's quick repair sends silt into the village wells and leaves the miller blamed for every drought.
material: The sluice gate is warped and shedding iron pins.
testimony: The miller says upstream owners demanded a higher flow.
covenant: A submerged mark names the well as a shared obligation.

options.name: Rebuild the gate
options.term: The mill must publish its water turns and fund well clearing.
options.effect: Power returns, with a public schedule that can be challenged.

options.name: Retire the channel
options.term: Repay the mill workers and restore the older stream bed.
options.effect: The wells clear, while flour must arrive by road for a season.

title: The Quarry Cut
problem: A new cut shortens the road but shakes loose the boundary ridge above a hamlet.
material: Fresh cracks run from the cut to the houses.
testimony: The quarry crews were paid to ignore the smaller slips.
covenant: The ridge marks forbid taking stone beyond the old line.

options.name: Brace the cut
options.term: Cap extraction and put the hamlet on the inspection council.
options.effect: The shortcut survives under strict limits and slower stone output.

options.name: Close and reroute
options.term: Fund a longer road and restitution for displaced workers.
options.effect: The ridge settles; caravans travel farther and the quarry loses work.

title: The Witness Anchor
problem: An old road anchor fails as two communities disagree over who can speak for the Wild.
material: The anchor's iron collar is sound; the stone below has moved.
testimony: Both communities preserved different halves of the renewal rite.
covenant: The erased clause requires witnesses from both sides of the road.

options.name: Renew the bounds
options.term: Limit further settlement and restore the two-sided rite.
options.effect: The anchor quiets, but promised new holdings cannot open.

options.name: Negotiate a new term
options.term: Name local witnesses and publish a review date for expansion.
options.effect: The road remains open under a fragile, revisable compact.

title: The Last Circuit
problem: Wayside must decide what its roads permit when the final renewal circuit fails.
material: The circuit links every repaired site; the weakest span bears the load.
testimony: Each community asks that its losses appear in the final record.
covenant: No one witness can bind every road without consent.

options.name: Public road charter
options.term: Create inspected institutions with restitution and appeal rights.
options.effect: The charter can coordinate repairs, but its authority needs constant restraint.

options.name: Living local accord
options.term: Bind a shared minimum with each community able to revisit its terms.
options.effect: The roads endure through negotiation, at the cost of speed and certainty.
